## User Story

As a consumer of peer-review audit evidence
I want to know whether a model attribution is independently observed or merely declared
So that an incorrect model declaration cannot masquerade as verified runtime provenance

## Scope

Incident label: `incident:peer-review-56`. Source incident: #56, 2026-09-14.

Execution authorization from the user: implement these five diagnosed defects serially, delivering each one to trunk before starting the next; **no plan and no review**. Do not create specification/implementation-plan artifacts, run design/code/peer reviews, dispatch reviewers, or invoke any paid provider. This explicit exception overrides planning and review requirements for this incident series only. Retain focused regression tests, applicable repository checks, issue tracking, truthful evidence, and safe Git delivery. Never fabricate plan/review acceptance or bypass a hard tool refusal; if a workflow cannot represent the authorized exception, report the exact blocker instead of inventing evidence.

Preserve the incident worktree `/Users/kpburson/projects/Vibe-Coding/ai-peer-review-worktrees/56-macos-broker-endpoint` exactly: HEAD `ea599d7c65341a4754a1ed97d7b7ba97be262ae2`, dirty design, all fifteen scratch review workspaces and all review collateral. Do not resume #56, #39, or #43; do not submit recovery 14 or create recovery 15. Implement from current trunk in a separate issue worktree. Do not import the incident branch or its design revisions.

Series position: 5 of 5. Deliver only after all earlier incident series positions have landed on trunk.

Make model provenance truthful independently of genuine session identity. Runtime model attribution needs supported authoritative evidence; caller-supplied model environment alone must not imply independent verification. Detect conflicts when authoritative runtime observations are available, and retain explicit honest fallback when unavailable.

Serial delivery prerequisite: #60 must be delivered to trunk and closed through the authorized workflow before implementation of this defect begins.

## Reproduction

The incident Codex runtime turn contexts record gpt-5.6-sol. All fifteen review-created events record author model gpt-6-astra / GPT-6 Astra with identity_source runtime. The author commands explicitly supplied CODEX_MODEL_ID=gpt-6-astra and CODEX_MODEL_DISPLAY=GPT-6 Astra. A pure adapter probe reproduces source:runtime using only caller-supplied model environment.

## Root Cause

`src/identity/codex.mjs:5-12` accepts model IDs/displays from environment and returns source:runtime without independent model verification. The actual session can be genuine while model attribution is incorrect; do not conflate these two assurances or claim the provider/session separation was absent.

## Fix Direction

Represent session and model evidence at the assurance actually established. Use supported authoritative observations where available and an explicitly declared/unverified fallback otherwise. Refuse conflicting verified observations; preserve backward readability without retroactively elevating or rewriting old evidence.

## Out of Scope

Rewriting the fifteen incident records; replacing session fingerprints; general-purpose cryptographic attestation; provider launch bootstrap; billing/model-price lookup.

## Story Origin

Created at the user's explicit request after a sequential, read-only diagnosis of the #56 peer-review incident. No implementation plan or peer-review acceptance is claimed or required for this series under the user's explicit exception.

Evidence baseline: incident worktree HEAD `ea599d7c65341a4754a1ed97d7b7ba97be262ae2`; original review `review-4cfb5f9f356de98531af24241169ebfb`; current unsubmitted recovery 14 `review-b04b8234072da6949eab6e2f5d6ddc74`. Source paths below refer to that baseline and must be relocated against current trunk. Relevant source was unchanged from the original artifact commit `c03814267c704f89c554ce57626a1d87896bf4a3` through the baseline.

**Authority**: `.scratch/peer-review/review-*/events.jsonl`, `protocol.json`, `provider/claude/launch-state.json`, and sealed response Markdown under `docs/peer-reviews/spec/`. Private provider transcripts were inspected locally; do not publish raw session handles, credentials, or full transcripts. Scratch response JSON retains draft metadata; establish submission from events and sealed Markdown.

## Plan Metadata

- Implementation authority: the issue Scope, Root Cause, Fix Direction, and governed Deep-Dive Analysis below.
- Corrective authority: the retrospective external Claude review of merged PR #80, recorded in the issue timeline.
- Delivery gate: a corrective pull request must pass hosted CI and a fresh external Claude review of its exact head before merge.
- Standalone plan artifact: none; the issue Deep-Dive Analysis is the executable implementation plan for this bounded defect.

## Pickup Directive — MANDATORY, DO NOT SKIP

> Follow: `.ai-task-manager/templates/pickup-directive.md`

## Deep-Dive Analysis (2026-09-19)

> Mirrored from comment #issuecomment-5744115940 (https://github.com/kburson/ai-peer-review/issues/61#issuecomment-5744115940). Comment is the diff-history canonical; this body copy is the gate-canonical source.

### Files examined and changed

- `src/identity/codex.mjs` and `src/identity/registry.mjs` for declared versus observed model identity.
- `src/protocol/compatibility.mjs`, `src/protocol/service.mjs`, `src/protocol/events.mjs`, and `src/protocol/reducer.mjs` for compatible v1-to-v2 event persistence.
- `src/cli/run.mjs` for production start, join, refresh, replacement, and retry paths.
- `schemas/manifest-v1.json` and participant schemas for backward-readable manifest evidence.
- Unit and integration tests covering model provenance, start/join, submission, supersession, and v2 dormancy.

### Root-cause confirmation

The first implementation rendered provenance evidence but production writers still projected participants through the v1 shape, stripping that evidence before persistence. The integration fixture bypassed those writers, and making `evidence` required in the unchanged v1 manifest schema broke archived manifests. The retrospective Claude review of merged PR #80 exposed these gaps.

### Implementation sequence

1. Preserve the legacy v1 genesis event, then introduce the current compatibility declaration before the first v2 event so sequence numbers remain deterministic.
2. Emit v2 participant evidence from production identity-change, reviewer-join, and participant-replacement paths while keeping retry comparisons compatible with legacy v1 projections.
3. Keep `evidence` optional in `manifest-v1` and use the canonical participant-v2 evidence reference so archived v1 manifests remain valid.
4. Exercise the real production writers in integration tests instead of injecting a v2 fixture that production could not emit.
5. Run every issue verification command in an isolated exact-SHA Test worktree, then require hosted CI and an exact-head external Claude review before merge.

### Test additions and updates

- `test/unit/model-provenance.test.mjs`: declaration-only, authoritative-observation, and conflict semantics.
- `test/unit/manifest.test.mjs`: archived v1 compatibility and the participant-v2 evidence reference.
- `test/integration/model-provenance.test.mjs`: production persistence and presentation of provenance evidence.
- `test/integration/start-join.test.mjs`, `submit.test.mjs`, `supersession-lineage.test.mjs`, and `v2-dormancy.test.mjs`: compatible sequence and retry behavior across existing flows.

The root Acceptance Criteria and Verification Commands remain the authoritative checklists; this appendix does not duplicate them.

### Risks and mitigations

- Event insertion could corrupt sequence numbers; service-level compatibility insertion and integration coverage constrain the ordering.
- New evidence could break legacy readers; the v1 manifest keeps evidence optional and legacy projections remain readable.
- Retry equality could become evidence-sensitive; comparisons deliberately project through the stable v1 participant identity fields.
- A fixture-only success could recur; the regression tests now enter through production start and identity writers.

### Dependency map

Depends on: #60, already delivered and closed before #61 implementation began.

Blocks: #56, whose preserved incident worktree resumes only after #61 reaches Done.

- `schemas/manifest-v1.json` and participant schemas for backward-readable manifest evidence.
- Unit and integration tests covering model provenance, start/join, submission, supersession, and v2 dormancy.

### Root-cause confirmation

The first implementation rendered provenance evidence but production writers still projected participants through the v1 shape, stripping that evidence before persistence. The integration fixture bypassed those writers, and making `evidence` required in the unchanged v1 manifest schema broke archived manifests. The retrospective Claude review of merged PR #80 exposed these gaps.

### Implementation sequence

1. Preserve the legacy v1 genesis event, then introduce the current compatibility declaration before the first v2 event so sequence numbers remain deterministic.
2. Emit v2 participant evidence from production identity-change, reviewer-join, and participant-replacement paths while keeping retry comparisons compatible with legacy v1 projections.
3. Keep `evidence` optional in `manifest-v1` and use the canonical participant-v2 evidence reference so archived v1 manifests remain valid.
4. Exercise the real production writers in integration tests instead of injecting a v2 fixture that production could not emit.
5. Run every issue verification command in an isolated exact-SHA Test worktree, then require hosted CI and an exact-head external Claude review before merge.

### Test additions and updates

- `test/unit/model-provenance.test.mjs`: declaration-only, authoritative-observation, and conflict semantics.
- `test/unit/manifest.test.mjs`: archived v1 compatibility and the participant-v2 evidence reference.
- `test/integration/model-provenance.test.mjs`: production persistence and presentation of provenance evidence.
- `test/integration/start-join.test.mjs`, `submit.test.mjs`, `supersession-lineage.test.mjs`, and `v2-dormancy.test.mjs`: compatible sequence and retry behavior across existing flows.

The root Acceptance Criteria and Verification Commands remain the authoritative checklists; this appendix does not duplicate them.

### Risks and mitigations

- Event insertion could corrupt sequence numbers; service-level compatibility insertion and integration coverage constrain the ordering.
- New evidence could break legacy readers; the v1 manifest keeps evidence optional and legacy projections remain readable.
- Retry equality could become evidence-sensitive; comparisons deliberately project through the stable v1 participant identity fields.
- A fixture-only success could recur; the regression tests now enter through production start and identity writers.
